title: Simultaneous exact-adjoint K-injective tower and normalized Roos models
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites in one universe, $R,S$ sheaves of rings, not necessarily commutative, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ and $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive functors with $F\dashv G$ and $F$ exact (preserving short exact sequences). Write $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$, and likewise for $\mathcal B$, with levelwise exactness, and let $G^{\rm Tow}$ apply $G$ levelwise. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories with localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and total right derived functors with universal units, computed on K-injectives [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. A complex is K-injective when every chain map from an acyclic complex to it is null-homotopic.
For every strict tower complex $X$ there is a quasi-isomorphism $q:X\to I$ with $I$ K-injective and every $I^r$ injective in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$. For every such choice put $J=G^{\rm Tow}I$, $P_I=\prod_n I_n$, $P_J=\prod_n GI_n$, $L_I=\lim_n I_n$ and $L_J=\lim_n GI_n$, all termwise. Then $J$ is K-injective with injective degree terms; all $I_n,GI_n,L_I,L_J,P_I,P_J,G(L_I),G(P_I)$ are K-injective. Under the derived-functor units, $QJ$, $Q(L_I)$ and $Q(L_J)$ compute respectively $R(G^{\rm Tow})(QX)$, $R\lim_{\mathcal A}(QX)$ and $R\lim_{\mathcal B}(R(G^{\rm Tow})(QX))$, and $Q(G(L_I))$ computes $RG(R\lim_{\mathcal A}(QX))$. The products $QP_I$ and $QP_J$ represent the respective countable derived products.
The degreewise canonical comparisons are natural chain isomorphisms
$$c:G(P_I)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_J,\qquad\beta:G(L_I)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_J,$$
characterized by $\pi_n c=G(\pi_n)$ and $\lambda_n\beta=G(\lambda_n)$. The analogous comparisons are chain isomorphisms for every tower complex, without K-injectivity. Under the preceding unit identifications, $Q(c)$ is the derived product comparison with components $RG(p_n)$. For $s_I,s_J$ induced by the strict transitions [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism],
$$cG(s_I)=s_Jc,\qquad cG(1-s_I)=(1-s_J)c.$$
All comparisons are natural for strict tower chain maps and their localized morphisms between K-injective representatives. The preceding assertions do not require exact countable products. If countable products in both module categories are exact, put $H_T=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_T)[-1]$ for $T=I,J$, with coordinates $(y,x)$ as in [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. The inclusions $j_T:L_T\to H_T$, $z\mapsto(0,(\lambda_nz)_n)$, are quasi-isomorphisms. For the unit-normalized comparison $\kappa_T:Q(H_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim(QT)$ obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-exact-products-roos-comparison] by the chain sign isomorphism $(y,x)\mapsto(-y,x)$ from the fibre of $-(1-s_T)$, one has $\kappa_T Q(j_T)=\eta^{\lim}_T$. Here $\eta^{\lim}$ is the universal derived-limit unit; on the K-injective $T$ it identifies $Q(L_T)$ with $R\lim(QT)$. In particular transporting the rotated cone triangle $(H_T,P_T,P_T;r,1-s_T,b)$ along $Q(j_T)$ gives the unit-normalized Roos triangle, where $r(y,x)=x$ and $b(z)=(z,0)$.
